title: Song of Solomon Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Song of Solomon 4: hair like a flock of goats, a neck like David's tower, a locked garden, and streams from Lebanon.

questions.text: From which mountain do the goats descend, in the comparison with the bride's hair?
questions.explanation: He says, "Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead."

questions.text: To what are the bride's teeth compared?
questions.explanation: Her teeth are like a newly shorn flock which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins.

answers.text: A string of pearls from the deep sea
A newly shorn flock come up from the washing
A row of smooth white stones by the brook
Two pieces of a ripe pomegranate behind a veil

questions.text: What are the bride's lips like, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: He says, "Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely."

questions.text: The bride's neck is like David's tower. What hangs on that tower?
questions.explanation: Her neck is like David's tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.

questions.text: After praising her, what does the beloved say about any spot in his love?
questions.explanation: He says, "You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you."

answers.text: One small spot remains in her
There is no spot in her
Her spots are covered by her veil
The washing has removed every spot

questions.text: From where does the beloved call his bride to come with him?
questions.explanation: He says, "Come with me from Lebanon, my bride," and to look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon.

questions.text: What is under the bride's tongue, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: He says, "Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue."

questions.text: How does the beloved describe his sister, his bride, in verse 12?
questions.explanation: He says, "My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain."

answers.text: An open field of lilies in the valleys
A vineyard in blossom on the hillsides
A locked up garden and a sealed fountain
A city with high walls and strong towers

questions.text: From where do the flowing streams of the "well of living waters" come?
questions.explanation: The bride is called a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.

questions.text: What are the north wind and the south wind told to do at the end of the chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says, "Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out."

answers.text: To carry the voice of the beloved over the hills
To scatter the flock of goats on the mountain
To blow on the garden, that its spices may flow out
To bring the rain back upon the vineyards
